correctness.rationale: For all Latin squares M of n>=2, each graph edge has exactly one row/column/symbol line type; a non-line triangle is a rainbow triangle bijective with a missing (r,c,s), giving n²(n−1) such triangles. Its only possible extension to a 4-clique is its uniquely determined intercalate corner; each intercalate tetrahedron has free rainbow facets and no higher nonline cofaces. The cover of the 3n full line simplices has contractible intersections and nerve L containing the n² present triples in J=D_n*D_n*D_n; attaching all missing rainbow triangles gives Z homotopy equivalent to J (carrier-and-attachment homotopy step). Hence π1(Z)=0. Collapsing each tetrahedron and free rainbow facet gives a simply connected 2-dimensional CW model, χ=1+(n−1)^3−I(M), integral H_2 free of this rank, so Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give a wedge of that many S². Direct independent face-count checks: n=2,I=1, rank0; n=3,I=0,rank8; n=4 cyclic I=4,rank23 and Klein-four I=12,rank15. Finite counts corroborate but do not prove the nerve comparison or infinite family; no equivariance is asserted.

value.rationale: The homotopy type of a natural family of strongly regular graph clique complexes is not determined by all-field Betti numbers: π1 and attaching maps matter. This uniform simply-connected 2D model across even, nongroup and small orders is a substantive classification, not a mere restatement of the rank formula.

limitations: Ordinary homotopy only, n>=2, no canonical equivariant basis or automorphism module; finite tests not a universal proof.
